question: A 27-year-old bus driver narrowly survived a major RTA 18 days ago. He presents with intrusive nightmares, flashbacks when driving, emotional numbing, and hypervigilance. Symptoms began within days of the accident. What is the MOST appropriate diagnosis at this point?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: PTSD requires symptoms persisting for MORE than 1 month after the traumatic event. At 18 days, the 1-month threshold has not yet been met — do not apply a PTSD diagnosis at this stage.

Correct. ASD is diagnosed when PTSD-like symptoms (re-experiencing, avoidance, hyperarousal, dissociation) occur between 3 days and 1 month after trauma. At 18 days with onset within days of the accident, ASD is the correct label.

Adjustment disorder involves a disproportionate emotional response to an identifiable stressor but does NOT include intrusive re-experiencing or hyperarousal clusters. The presence of flashbacks and nightmares points toward ASD/PTSD, not adjustment disorder.

GAD requires ≥6 months of pervasive worry unlinked to a specific traumatic event. This presentation is directly tied to a discrete trauma with a re-experiencing cluster, making GAD inappropriate here.

overallFeedback.feedback: Use the timeline-first approach: ASD = 3 days to 1 month post-trauma; PTSD = symptoms persist beyond 1 month. Adjustment disorder lacks the re-experiencing/flashback cluster.
Correct. The 3-day–1-month window and post-trauma re-experiencing cluster define ASD. The same symptom pattern lasting >1 month would meet PTSD criteria.
